name: Raiju
description: Raiju (雷獣, 'thunder beast') is a legendary yōkai from Japanese mythology, the companion of Raijin the thunder god, whose body is composed of or wrapped in lightning. It descends during thunderstorms, becomes agitated, and may take many animal forms — most often a weasel, wolf, or cat — depending on the regional tradition.

aliases.name: Raijuu
aliases.meaning: Alternative Hepburn romanization of the same term

origin: Raiju legends are primarily concentrated in East Japan, with notable regional variants throughout the Japanese archipelago. Most documented accounts come from the Edo period, with locations including Akita, Shinano, Echigo, Sagami, Aizu, Lake Biwa, and Akō.
